title: APPENDIX: A SUPPLEMENTAL HISTORY
text:
16        APPENDIX: A SUPPLEMENTAL HISTORY

On motion of Gus W. Thomassen a fund was started with which to underwrite the cost of printing Miss Mattie Lee Boyd's Supplemental History of Savoy College. The motion prevailed that the book be printed as and when funds were available, and that, in the meantime, the Board of Managers take the matter under advisement, study the needs and take whatever action might be deemed advisable, being thus given full power and authority to act.

By request, Mrs. Guy P. Harris sang, "When You and I Were Young, Maggie." She, then, led the audience in singing, "Auld Lang Syne," whereupon, the meeting adjourned.

AD INTERIM REUNIONS AND BOARD MEETINGS

A number of meetings have been held by the Board of Managers during 1939-1943 inclusive, while in preparation of this book. Each member of the board has assumed a specific task in getting things done. Several joint meetings have been held by the Board with members of an Advisory Committee, a volunteer group of ex-students, living conveniently near each other, who have met on call for the purpose, in connection with plans for the book project. The first meeting was held with Mrs. James A. (Beulah Thomassen) Stinnett at her home in Van Alstyne, on December 28, 1941. Others met there at this first meeting, and several general plans were formulated. The second meeting was also in December (December 29, 1942) at Savoy, at the Edgar and Ed McMahon families acting jointly as hosts, at the former's home, when final plans for the printing of book were completed.

The small group meetings have been held each year since and have come to be called by those in attendance "little reunions," and, as such, have been enormously enjoyed. Ex-students' families and friends occasionally attend and by the former have been dubbed "insiders and outlaws," the former meaning kinship and the latter friendship.
